countries.summary: Singapore paused approvals for new large-scale data centres from 2019 to 2022, as described by Reed Smith and by a 2022 EDB/IMDA-based report. Since then, capacity has been released through competitive Calls for Application: a 2022 pilot (DC-CFA) and a second round (DC-CFA2) with a green-energy condition, under which 200 MW was provisionally allocated on 21 August 2026. Only EDB's release is quoted here; the operator-level figures are in the notes and not yet verified against the fact sheet.

In Quebec, the government requires authorization before any new load or load addition of 5 MW or more can be connected. Hydro-Quebec has applied to the Regie de l'energie for a dedicated large data-centre rate of about 13 cents per kWh; that proceeding is open, with hearings scheduled for October and December 2026. The Quebec government decree the application cites (89-2026) is not yet verified against the Gazette.

Project Mars (Lane Cove) is reported as withdrawn; this was not verified on a primary page.

fields.title: Data Centre Call for Application (DC-CFA) pilot, 2022
fields.status_detail: Pilot call launched July 2022; application window closed 21 Nov 2022. Awards announced 2023.
fields.summary: The pilot Call for Application for new green data-centre capacity was launched by EDB and IMDA after the 2019–2022 pause was lifted. It required PUE of 1.3 or better and Platinum certification under the BCA-IMDA Green Mark.
key_terms: The pilot DC-CFA application will close on 21 November 2022.

records.source_title: w.media — EDB & IMDA to launch a pilot Data Centre Call For Application (DC-CFA) for building sustainable DC
records.verbatim: The pilot DC-CFA application will close on 21 November 2022.
records.notes: Article dated 20 Jul 2022 (per fetched page); this reproduces the agencies' pilot announcement, not the EDB/IMDA page itself. Eligibility quoted from the same page: PUE "of 1.3 (at 100% IT load) or better" and Platinum Green Mark. The 2022 article gives no MW range; search snippets citing 10–30 MW and a maximum of three approvals were not verified and are not used. Outcome conflict to resolve: Pinsent Masons (7 Sep 2026) says "the 80MW allocated under the first call for application which was launched in 2022"; a search summary cited an IMDA figure of about 120 MW of IT load. Neither is stored. Reed Smith gives the same ~80 MW to four operators. No primary IMDA award document was fetched.

fields.duration_description: Approx. 2019 to 2022 (about three years); lifted 2022 with conditions.
fields.summary: A de facto moratorium on new large-scale data-centre approvals ran from 2019 to 2022. No published decision set it; it is described after the fact. It was lifted in 2022 with conditions and replaced by a competitive Call for Application (DC-CFA). Key reasons are not yet verified and are left empty.

records.source_title: Reed Smith — Singapore's data centre expansion on Jurong Island: sustainable growth
records.verbatim: From 2019 to 2022, Singapore maintained a de facto moratorium on new large-scale data centre approvals
records.notes: formality de_facto requires the authority's statement or two independent sources. Source 1: Reed Smith (fetched; verbatim above; also "In 2022, the moratorium was lifted"). Source 2: w.media 2022 reproduction of the EDB/IMDA pilot release (https://w.media/edb-imda-to-launch-a-pilot-data-centre-call-for-application-dc-cfa-for-building-sustainable-dc/): "Earlier this year, the moratorium was lifted but with conditions." That is two sources, but neither is an IMDA/EDB page of its own, so the IMDA/EDB statement is still outstanding. The status 'enacted' is a schema fit for a pause that took effect; the formality field is the honest marker. The 2026 datacentres.com article (29 Apr 2026, https://www.datacentres.com/news/singapore-lifts-data-centre-moratorium) calls it a "moratorium" and a "pause", and says it started in 2019, but it is not used as a source. Its "three-year pause" wording is not reconciled with the 2019 start.

fields.summary: Projects of 5 MW or more, including new loads and load additions, must obtain the Quebec government's authorization before they can be connected. This is the allocation gate that sits in front of Hydro-Quebec's proposed data-centre rate. The statute and regulation behind it were not fetched directly.
